subject: Relational operators
notes: Rule: 'NOT < is an abbreviation for NOT LESS THAN.' (cite.py --check 8.7.5.2 -> OK §8.7.5.2 6)). The grammar admits 'NOT <' (comparisonOperator alt) and MapOperator normalizes the concatenated token text (IS/THAN/TO stripped, NOT inverts) so 'NOT <' and 'NOT LESS THAN' map to the same C# operator; the >>IF evaluator's private copy is textually identical. Probe probe/relop/relpos.cob (A=5 vs B=3 and B=5, IF with every printed spelling, --std 2023 and 85): the symbol and word forms give identical truth values at both data points (AB TTTFFFFFF|TTTTTFFFFFTTT / AC FFFFFFTTT|TTTTTTTTTTFFF at both editions), all as derived from the rule. The covering golden positions START with 'NOT LESS THAN' and with 'NOT <' on the same key and derives the same record (AB02) for both.
